judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Product thumbnail for item 1438, inside a link whose text already names the product. The crop, and the 970px version of the same photo, show a blue motor shield on an Arduino wired to a stepper motor, two servos and two DC motors. That is what the alt text describes. The 'v2' in the alt and 'v3' in the product name is a naming mismatch, and 'steppers' is plural when one stepper is shown. Neither means the alt describes something absent, and the text still serves the image's purpose. The model's suggested fix only swaps v2 for v3.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the header search field (#search). The screenshot and snapshot show a visible magnifying-glass submit button (#searchBtn, accessible name 'Search') at the right end of the field, inside the same search form. The input takes its name from that button through aria-labelledby. This is sufficient technique G167, whose Example 1 is exactly a search field labelled by an adjacent magnifying-glass button, so 3.3.2 is met. The rule's claim that no button sits near the field is wrong given the data it had.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The link 'turn UP the TERROR!' sits in the orange Halloween alert banner. Its parent div.message reads 'The Halloween countdown has begun ... Are you ready to turn UP the TERROR!?', and the banner has role=alert, so the whole message is read with the link. That parent text is programmatically determined link context. Together with the link text, it tells the user the link leads to the Halloween promotion, and it does: the destination is 'Halloween 2026 : Shopping Guides'. The finding's claim that 'nothing around it' says where the link goes is contradicted by the ancestor text Rampa itself captured. The link text is vague on its own, but 2.4.4 accepts context, so this passes. Judged on the 2026-10-10 snapshot; the seasonal banner may change on the live site.
